memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When Nahor had lived 29 years, he became the father of Terah. After he became the father of Terah, Nahor lived 119 years and had other sons and daughters. After Terah had lived 70 years, he became the father of Abram, Nahor and Haran. - Gen 11:24-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
And now a name we recognise: Abram. Suddenly this long list of unfamiliar names arrives at the man God would call to be the father of a nation and the channel of blessing to the whole world. But notice - before Abram was ever called, God had been preparing his family line for generations. The call in chapter 12 does not come out of nowhere; God had been at work for centuries.

This is how God so often operates. Long before we see His hand, He is arranging things. The people He calls, the moments He uses, the doors He opens - these are the visible surface of a work that began long before. Nothing about Abram's call was hasty or accidental.

There is deep reassurance in this. God is never scrambling. He is never caught off guard. Before you knew Him, before you were even born, He was already at work preparing your life and your path. As Paul marvels, God "set me apart from my mother's womb" (Gal 1:15).

Whatever God is calling you to, know that He has been preparing for it far longer than you realise - preparing you, preparing circumstances, preparing the way. The genealogy that seemed like dry record-keeping was actually God laying the groundwork for the salvation of the world. He is laying groundwork in your life too, patiently and purposefully, long before you can see it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Can you look back and see God preparing things before you noticed?
- How does it comfort you that God is never caught off guard?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Faithful God, thank You that long before I see Your hand, You are already at work preparing the way. Help me trust Your patient, purposeful planning over my life, as You planned for Abram.
Amen.
